product: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, 600 W) and Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel kit

wins.need: More usable energy from a 288 Wh-class station
wins.claim: In the same test, it gave more usable energy than the Anker SOLIX C300 (both rated 288 Wh). 4X4 Australia lists the unit as 'Bluetti Elite 30' with 600 W AC output, which matches the V2; the Elite 30 mini is 300 W.
wins.figure: 265 Wh usable (92% of 288 Wh) vs 235 Wh (82%) for the Anker SOLIX C300
wins.who: 4X4 Australia (Dex Fulton, Colin Dedman), 13 units physically tested, published 2026-09-21

wins.claim: Ran the same 35 L fridge longer than the Anker SOLIX C300

wins.need: Recharging from a single 12 V-class panel or a car
wins.claim: Took more watts in than the Anker SOLIX C300 at a single-panel voltage and at alternator voltage
wins.figure: 148 W vs 97 W at 18 V; 108 W vs 98 W at 13.2 V

wins.need: AC power for small appliances at this size and price
wins.claim: Its rated AC output is twice that of the Anker SOLIX C300 and the Jackery Explorer 300, and it costs less than the C300 and about the same as the Jackery
wins.figure: 600 W rated (BLUETTI, $289.99) vs 300 W for the Anker SOLIX C300 ($429.99, us.ankersolix.com/products/c300) and 300 W for the Jackery Explorer 300 ($289, jackery.com/products/explorer-300-portable-power-station), all prices read 2026-11-15

wins.claim: Its solar input is twice the C300's 100 W, so a second panel or a 200 W panel can be added. The kit's 100 W panel uses half of that.
wins.figure: 200 W max solar (BLUETTI) vs 100 W max (Anker C300, per OutdoorGearLab's spec table)

wins.need: Keeping a router or modem online when the power cuts out
wins.claim: Measured UPS switchover matches the BLUETTI claim, and it ran a router-sized AC load for half a day. This does not beat rivals: Anker and Jackery both claim 10 ms switchover too.
wins.figure: Under 10 ms, measured on an oscilloscope (The Technology Man); 11 h 23 min at a 13 W load with AC-ECO off (Reefs.com)
wins.who: The Technology Man (Gidon, 2025-12-23) and Reefs.com (Danilo Ronchi, 2026-05-12)

wins.claim: Full from the wall in about an hour. Results differ between testers.
wins.figure: Full in 51 min, 80% in about 40 min (The Technology Man); full in 70 min at 380 W (Zelpio). OutdoorGearLab measured 63 min for the Anker C300.

weak.claim: High idle drain when the AC inverter is left on with Eco mode off. The measurements are well above BLUETTI's '4.5 W standby' claim.
weak.figure: About 19 W with AC on (100% to 19% in 12 h) and about 11 W with DC on (The Technology Man). A second tester measured about 11 W with AC on and about 7 W with DC on (Zelpio, https://www.zelpio.com/blog/bluetti-elite-30-v2-review/)

weak.claim: Struggles with motor start-up surges. BLUETTI's 1,500 W 'Lifting Power' works by lowering the output voltage, only suits resistive loads, and real output stays at 600 W or less. BLUETTI publishes no surge rating.
weak.figure: A 450 W air duster drew about 2,300 W at switch-on and overloaded the unit. The 300 W BLUETTI AC2A ran the same duster.

weak.claim: Battery capacity cannot be expanded. The EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus can, with a $149 EB300 extra battery (us.ecoflow.com/products/river-3-plus-smart-extra-battery, read 2026-11-15).
weak.figure: Fixed at 288 Wh vs up to 858 Wh on the RIVER 3 Plus

weak.claim: Heavier than the lightest stations of the same size
weak.figure: 4.3 kg (9.5 lb) vs 7.5 lb for the Jackery Explorer 300 (jackery.com, read 2026-11-15) and 7.3 lb for the BLUETTI Elite 30 mini (bluettipower.com, read 2026-11-15)

weak.claim: Panels cannot be wired in series. The station accepts only one 12 V-class panel string, so two of the usual 22–25 V Voc panels wired in series would exceed the limit. The manual I opened is the 230 V edition.
weak.figure: 12–28 V solar input; 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 28V'

weak.claim: The station-only box has no solar cable, so buyers of the bare station need an MC4-to-XT60 cable for any panel
weak.figure: Box contents: station, AC cable, car cable, grounding screw, manual

weak.claim: The on-screen watt reading is unreliable at low loads
weak.figure: Showed 0 W for a 13 W load and about 55 W for a measured 32 W load (Reefs.com). The Technology Man also found the readings run high because the unit ignores power factor.

weak.claim: The 100 W kit costs a lot per Wh of battery (arithmetic). BLUETTI's own Elite 30 mini + 100 W kit costs $80 less.
weak.figure: $489.99 / 288 Wh = $1.70 per Wh; the panel adds $200 over the $289.99 station; Elite 30 mini + 100 W is $409.99

wins_for: A weekend car or tent camper who wants one box with a panel included under $500, running phones, a laptop and a 12 V fridge (measured 25 h on a 35 L fridge, 4X4 Australia)
A shopper who needs AC power up to 600 W for small resistive appliances (not motors) from a station under 10 lb, for less than the 300 W Anker SOLIX C300 costs
A buyer who wants room to add more solar later (200 W input) without changing stations
Keeping a router or modem online through an outage with under 10 ms switchover, as long as AC-ECO is set correctly (11 h 23 min at 13 W, Reefs.com)
not_for: Home backup or a kitchen refrigerator: 288 Wh with no expansion, and a 450 W motor load overloaded it. Recommend the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro (768 Wh, 800 W, $369 at us.ecoflow.com, read 2026-11-15) or a larger BLUETTI such as the Elite 100 V2 or 200 V2.
RV use: too small, with no expansion and no series-wired solar. Recommend a 1–2 kWh station (our existing pick there is the Elite 200 V2).
Backpacking or the lightest possible carry: 9.5 lb. The Jackery Explorer 300 is 7.5 lb ($289) and the BLUETTI Elite 30 mini is 7.3 lb (its 100 W kit is $409.99).
Leaving the AC inverter on overnight for tiny loads: idle drain measured at 11–19 W. Use the 12 V DC outputs or Eco mode, or pick a station with lower measured idle draw.
Shoppers who want to add battery capacity later: the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus expands to 858 Wh

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Slightly lighter (9.1 lb measured by OutdoorGearLab vs 9.5 lb) and has two-way 140 W USB-C charging. In 4X4 Australia's test it lost on usable energy (235 vs 265 Wh), fridge runtime and solar input, and it is rated 300 W against our 600 W.

rivals.model: Anker SOLIX C300X DC with 60 W solar panel
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: $50 cheaper than our 60 W kit ($399.99), but it has no AC outlet (DC only)
$80 cheaper and 7.3 lb vs 9.5 lb, with the same 288 Wh. It is rated 300 W (600 W lifting) against our 600 W.

rivals.price: $289, station only, jackery.com/products/explorer-300-portable-power-station, from the store's search feed read 2026-11-15
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: 7.5 lb vs 9.5 lb, with 4,000+ cycles to 70% stated by Jackery. It is rated 300 W with 2 AC outlets.

rivals.price: Not priced: EcoFlow's US store returned HTTP 429 (see unsourced)
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Capacity can be expanded to 858 Wh with a $149 EB300 (us.ecoflow.com/products/river-3-plus-smart-extra-battery, read 2026-11-15)
768 Wh and 800 W for $369 ($0.48 per rated Wh vs $1.01 for our station, arithmetic), but it weighs 18.2 lb and claims under 30 ms EPS switchover
